definitions.explanation: A person who works aboard a ship, especially one engaged in manual labor on deck rather than in a commanding or navigating role. The word has a somewhat traditional or literary flavor.

examples.japanese: {水夫|すいふ}たちが{帆|ほ}を{張|は}った。
{祖父|そふ}は{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}、{水夫|すいふ}として{世界|せかい}を{回|まわ}った。
examples.english: My grandfather traveled around the world as a sailor when he was young.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{小説|しょうせつ}には、{嵐|あらし}と{闘|たたか}う{水夫|すいふ}たちの{姿|すがた}がよく{描|えが}かれている。
examples.english: Old novels often depict sailors battling storms.

notes:
A compound of {水|すい} (water) and {夫|ふ} (man, laborer). Also read as かこ in classical Japanese. The word evokes traditional seafaring and appears frequently in literature, historical accounts, and stories about the age of sail. In modern maritime usage, {船員|せんいん} or {乗組員|のりくみいん} are the standard terms for crew members.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水夫|すいふ}として{働|はたら}く: to work as a sailor
- {水夫|すいふ}を{雇|やと}う: to hire sailors
- {水夫|すいふ}{長|ちょう}: boatswain, chief deckhand

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {船員|せんいん}: crew member, seafarer — the modern, official term for anyone working aboard a ship
- {乗組員|のりくみいん}: crew member — used for the crew of ships, aircraft, or spacecraft
- {船|ふな}{乗|の}り: sailor, mariner — a slightly more colloquial word with a romantic or adventurous connotation
- {海員|かいいん}: seaman, maritime worker — a formal term used in labor law and maritime regulations
